chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:
I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'When I recite the Quran and raise my voice with it, Satan comes to me and says,
You are showing off with this to your family and the people.

He (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Muhammad! Recite a recitation that is between the two [extremes], making your family hear, and modulate your voice with the Quran, for indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves the beautiful voice in which modulation is performed.'

key_terms.بَيْنَ الْقِرَاءَتَيْنِ: Between the two [extremes of loudness and quietness]
key_terms.تَرْجِيع: Modulation or melodic variation of the voice
key_terms.رِيَاء: Showing off (performing acts for the sake of being seen by others)

ai.seo_question: How should one modulate their voice when reciting the Quran to avoid showing off and please Allah?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses the spiritual danger of riya' (showing off) associated with loud recitation, prescribing a 'middle way' that balances audibility for family with humility. This guidance reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on internal sincerity (ikhlas) over external display, linking the aesthetic quality of the voice to divine love. The recommendation to modulate the voice serves as a practical method for maintaining concentration (khushu') while avoiding the pitfalls of vanity.
